Register your own app at dev.twitch.tv with OAuth Redirect URL "http://localhost:17563/callback", then paste its Client ID/Secret here.

1. Go to dev.twitch.tv/console/apps and click "Register Your Application". 2. OAuth Redirect URL: http://localhost:17563/callback 3. Category: anything (e.g. "Application Integration"). 4. Save, copy the Client ID, then click "New Secret" for the Client Secret.
Register your own app at developer.spotify.com/dashboard with Redirect URI "http://127.0.0.1:17564/callback", then paste its Client ID/Secret here.

1. Go to developer.spotify.com/dashboard and click "Create app". 2. Redirect URI: http://127.0.0.1:17564/callback 3. Which API/SDKs are you planning to use: Web API. 4. Save, then copy the Client ID and click "View client secret" for the Client Secret.
Create an OAuth Desktop-app client at console.cloud.google.com with the YouTube Data API v3 enabled, then paste its Client ID/Secret here.

1. Go to console.cloud.google.com, create/select a project, then enable "YouTube Data API v3" (APIs & Services -> Library). 2. Open "Google Auth Platform" -> Branding: set an App name + support email (first run shows a "Get Started" wizard). 3. Audience tab: User type "External", then add your own Google account under "Test users". 4. Clients tab -> Create Client -> Application type: Desktop app -> Create. Copy the Client ID/Secret now — the secret is shown only once. 5. First sign-in shows "Google hasn't verified this app" (expected, sensitive scope) — click Advanced -> Go to your app (unsafe). In Testing status, sign-in may need repeating every ~7 days; "Publish app" in Audience avoids that.
The emoji is typed into the focused application when the key is pressed. On a display key (DisplayPad, Everest Max numpad) it is also used as the key image.
In the script use 'import k2' to call K2 functions (k2.log, k2.get_state, k2.switch_profile, k2.run_action, ...). stdout/stderr go to the K2 log.

Sign in above, then click Record action and perform the action on the page (turn on, dim, change colour…): K2 captures the command Google Home sends and replays it on a key press. "Record opposite action" adds the reverse to the selected binding, so one key alternates between the two.

Enables debug tools (driver open/close, AP controls, event log) on every device.

Drives the DisplayPad directly over USB instead of the Mountain SDK: confirmed transfers (no icon corruption), no satellite process. Profile persistence on the device is not available; images are re-uploaded from the K2 database. Takes effect after restarting K2.
Everest Max: native USB engine (experimental, partial)

Drives the Everest Max's connection and the 4 numpad display buttons directly over USB instead of SDKDLL.dll — removes that DLL's chronic timer-thread crash for what it covers. RGB effects, numpad icons, Media Dock, and full-keyboard remap events still use SDKDLL.dll for now (not yet ported). Takes effect after restarting K2.
Automatically stop Base Camp on startup

Every time K2 starts, it stops the Base Camp Windows service and closes every Base Camp process (GUI, service, workers, Makalu monitor) still running or relaunched by Windows autostart — so K2 fully replaces Base Camp instead of both running at once. Disable this if you still want to use Base Camp alongside K2.

MountainDisplayPadWorker runs in the background and writes to the DisplayPad at the same time as K2, corrupting icons. When enabled, K2 terminates it automatically (and keeps it closed while running).
Start Base Camp services with Windows
Enables/disables the Windows autostart entries of Base Camp (same mechanism as Task Manager's Startup tab — reversible). Entries in HKLM may require running K2 as administrator.
No Base Camp autostart entry found in the registry.
Restart Base Camp when K2 closes

When K2 closes, relaunches whatever Base Camp processes it auto-stopped (GUI, workers, Makalu monitor, the Windows service) — so Base Camp is back the way it was before K2 started. MountainDisplayPadWorker is always relaunched silently, with no window. Disabled by default: most people who enable auto-stop want Base Camp to stay stopped after closing K2.
Copies the current K2.App log (and crash log, if any) to a folder you choose — handy for sharing when reporting a problem.

Looks for an existing Base Camp installation and offers to import its profiles and settings for every K2 device (Everest Max, Everest 60, Makalu, MacroPad, DisplayPad). Shown automatically the first time K2 runs — use this button to run it again any time.

A Base Camp installation was detected on this PC. Would you like to import its existing profiles and settings into K2? You'll get a chance to review what's found for each connected device before anything is imported.

MacroPad, Everest Max and Everest 60 rely on a few native DLLs that are internal Base Camp components and are NOT distributed with K2 (MacroPadSDK.dll, SDKDLL.dll, Everest360_USB.dll). Either use a detected Base Camp installation, or point K2 at a folder containing the DLLs.

Close to tray instead of exiting

K2 now requires administrator rights (to control BaseCampService). Windows does not auto-elevate apps launched from the Run registry key at logon, so this entry alone may fail to start K2 silently — if that happens, use Task Scheduler instead (a task set to "Run with highest privileges" at logon).
K2 starts with its drivers active but the window hidden in the tray — open it anytime from the tray icon.

If you moved a DisplayPad to a different USB port and its saved profiles now show up on the wrong panel (e.g. "DisplayPad 2" and "DisplayPad 3" swapped), use this to reassign which panel each connected pad is treated as.

Reset all settings to factory default

Erases the keyboard's own memory — firmware profiles, key bindings, display-key images and lighting — and clears K2's saved configuration for it. Not the same as the sidebar's "Restore defaults", which only resets K2's profiles and leaves the device untouched.

This wipes the keyboard's own memory back to factory state: every firmware profile, key binding, display-key image and lighting effect stored on the device is erased, and K2's saved configuration for this keyboard is deleted to match. Afterwards K2 only restarts the keyboard's lighting with the first effect of the list — nothing else is pushed back to the device. This cannot be undone. Continue?
